DONE, and the live project turned out to be OneDrive-SYNCED AND PRESENT ON THE LAPTOP (%USERPROFILE%/OneDrive - Opal Capital/Shared - Documents/OCIO Models/Dashboard/202511 Model Portfolio Exposure), so the spec is read from Yang's own code rather than inferred. THE PULL: dc_return={price:PX_LAST, return:DAY_TO_DAY_TOT_RETURN_GROSS_DVDS} + dc_characteristic={name:NAME, fee:FUND_EXPENSE_RATIO, aum:FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS, num_holdings:TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HOLDINGS_IN_PORT, te:TRACKING_ERROR, yield:EQY_DVD_YLD_IND_NET, duration:HB_OAS_EFF_DURTN, credit:YAS_ISPREAD_TO_GOVT, beta:BETA_ADJ_OVERRIDABLE}, via tia BbgDataManager.get_historical, daily, over date_end=BDay(-1) back to YearEnd(-6) = ~6 YEARS. PROVEN to be the Positioning source by TIE-OUT: 7 of the 9 dc_characteristic KEYS are verbatim field names in the served current_holdings[] rows (aum/beta/credit/duration/fee/name/yield), num_holdings at book level, only te pulled-not-served. CORRECTION RECORDED: an earlier draft read the project README as 'holdings come from YCharts templates', which invites the false conclusion that YCharts is a data source for the page; Andrew corrected it -- the Positioning DATA is Bloomberg via Yang's pipeline, and the Excel is OUR OWN model composition (usecols=[0,1,2] = Date/Ticker/Weight) supplying WEIGHTS ONLY. That distinction is load-bearing: weights are ours, characteristics are Bloomberg's -- and for the ETFs we ALREADY own the weights. KEY ENGINEERING FINDING (the grain changes): model books hold FUNDS, ETF books hold SINGLE STOCKS, so 4 of the 9 characteristic fields are fund-only (FUND_EXPENSE_RATIO / FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS / TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HOLDINGS_IN_PORT / TRACKING_ERROR) and return correctly-empty on a stock -- 5 of 9 transfer unchanged; the fund-only four are still run against the 4 FUND tickers where they feed the book-level characteristics{} block. A naive re-point would read as a Bloomberg failure and is a category error.
